text:
Sam: FYI vendor pushed H200 lead times to 20-26 weeks. Just got the email.
Maya: Oof. Any confirmed windows on our open POs? @procurement
John: We have PO-4521 (40 units, eu-west) ETA Aug 15 (est), PO-4599 (20 units, us-central) ETA Sep 2. Both still "estimated".
Priya: If H200s are delayed, what are the fallback options? H100s? L40S?
Ana: L40S looks available faster in APAC (vendor quoted 8-10wks for ap-southeast). H100 lead time is ~12-16wks right now.
Victor: Proposal: reserve H200s only for the two low-latency clusters, move mixed/async to H100 or L40S. Can we reclassify routes to reduce H200 demand?
Maya: We need numbers. John, can you run a GPU-hours forecast by route and mark candidates to shift off H200? EOD Wed?
John: Doing a quick sketch now.
- Realtime-critical (H200 pinned): 120k GPU-hrs/month
- Mixed (can be flexible): 80k GPU-hrs/month
- Batch/embeddings: 220k GPU-hrs/month
If we shift 40% of mixed -> other hardware, frees ~32k H200 GPU-hrs/month.
Priya: Cost context: H200 reserved ~1.9x H100; L40S ~0.45x H200. But L40S may need int8 tuning; potential accuracy drift.
Sam: Also network concerns. eu-west1 inter-rack oversubscription showing higher tail latencies during spikes. Consolidating batch away could help.
Ana: Note: eu-west1 egress sustained capacity is ~1.2Tbps burst. If traffic grows as forecasted, quota bump needed; vendor says EU quota increases take 2-3 weeks.
Victor: Open quota tickets now then. Ana, can you file for EU and APAC egress increases?
Ana: Filed. devops-bot updated: Ticket #4287 for eu-west1 (assigned to Ana). Vendor response ETA 2-3 business days.
procurement-bot: Procurement flagged PO-4521 and PO-4599. Asked vendor about partial shipments and earlier splits.
Sam: Contingency: fund short-term H100 on-demand rentals for a 4-week surge if H200s slip. Cost ~2.5x reserved H200 but immediate.
Priya: I'll measure emergency H100 rental cost for 4-week window and run perf checks for L40S (int8 path, eval suite).
Maya: Also look at software fixes to reduce GPU-hours: KV-cache TTL increase, prompt trimming, more aggressive dynamic batching.
John: We have a runtime change that trims prompts and boosts cache TTLs; proto tests show ~12% reduction in avg seq length -> could save ~15k GPU-hrs/month.
Ana: Runtime note: enabling continuous batching on mixed clusters increases throughput but slightly worsens 95th for tiny requests. Canary required.
Sam: Canary rule: any change that worsens 95th by >5% needs explicit approval and staged rollout.
Victor: Timeline: 2 weeks to a Q3 plan with: reservation swaps/partials, quota requests, emergency rental budget, and list of routes to reclassify. Feasible?
Maya: Yes if procurement moves quickly and John delivers projections.
John: I'll upload the detailed projection sheet and region risk rows (APAC customs + eu-west1 egress pressure + us-central cost premium).
Sam: Product to mark critical vs flexible routes; we'll prioritize accordingly.
Priya: I'll start L40S evals on top-5 models tomorrow and report regressions.
Maya: Action items recap:
1) John: GPU-hrs forecast + candidate routes to move (EOD Wed)
2) Ana: Open/track egress quota tickets for eu-west1 & APAC (today)
3) Procurement: ask vendor for partial shipments and earlier splits (sam@proc)
4) Priya: L40S perf/regression checks + rental cost estimate (start tomorrow)
John: Uploaded projection: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/q3-capacity-projections
Sam: Reconvene Tue 09:30 PT with draft Q3 capacity plan.
devops-bot: Ticket #4287 opened for eu-west1 network quota (assigned: Ana).
procurement-bot: PO-4521 and PO-4599 matched to vendor ETA windows; procurement requested partial-shipment options.
Maya: Drop PO updates into this thread as they come. :thumbsup:
